answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake costly, verifiable work before earning reputation, like a garden that only grows in real soil. Instead of trusting cheap self-asserted identities, the network checks contributions anchored in basalt-hard proof: completed tasks with auditable outcomes, vouched for by peers whose own standing would crack like shale if they endorsed a fake. Newcomers start near zero trust and must earn their place through repeated, verifiable work, so spawning thousands of sock puppets buys nothing without slow, costly labor.
